# xg2g PSI (PAT/PMT/descriptor) corpus, format version 1
#
# Generated. To change it, edit psiCorpusCases() in
# backend/internal/stream/ingest/mediafacts/psi_corpus_test.go and run
#   go test ./internal/stream/ingest/mediafacts/ -run TestPSICorpus -update-psi-corpus
#
# A case is a core constructed with a target program number, then a sequence of
# calls. Each call is followed by the PSI-scoped part of the ParseResult it must
# produce:
#
#   chunk <hex>   one Ingest of these bytes, at the offset the previous chunks reached
#   target <n>    one SetTargetProgram
#   facts ...     the scalar facts after that call, and ProcessedThroughOffset
#   track ...     one line per audio track, in the order the PMT declares them
#   events ...    the event kinds that call produced, in order
#   psi ...       the raw ActivePSI packets, named by their index in the case's
#                 own packet sequence: packet N is bytes [188N, 188N+188) of the
#                 case's chunks concatenated
#
# Chunk boundaries are part of the case: a section assembler carries a partial
# section across a call, so the same packets cut differently are a different
# input.
#
# No case carries video elementary stream payload, so no case produces a random
# access point. Video facts here are the ones the PMT alone declares.
#
# A `note` on a case marks an expectation that records what the Go reference does
# today without a decision having been taken that it is what it should do.
version 1

case pat_then_pmt_in_one_chunk
  desc the PAT names the PMT PID and the PMT names the streams; each is one identity change
  init target=1
  chunk 
  facts through=376 hasPAT=1 hasPMT=1 pmtVersion=0 programNumber=1 pmtPID=256 videoPID=257 videoCodec=h264 audioPIDs=258
  track pid=258 streamType=6 codec=ac3 lang=deu channels=2 multichannel=0 componentType=2 hasComponentType=1
  events identity identity
  psi pat=0 pmt=1
end

case switching_the_target_program_discards_everything_about_the_old_one
  desc a zap to another service on the same transport keeps no fact from the service left behind
  note programNumber still reports the program that was just discarded, because SetTargetProgram clears neither pmtProgramNumber nor pmtVersion. See the stale-fact case below; this line records the defect, it does not bless it.

  chunk

  events identity identity
  psi pat=0 pmt=1
  target 2
  facts through=0 hasPAT=0 hasPMT=0 pmtVersion=0 programNumber=1 pmtPID=0 videoPID=0 videoCodec=unknown audioPIDs=
  events identity
  psi pat= pmt=

  events identity identity

end

case a_target_switch_leaves_the_old_program_number_and_version_behind
  desc the fields SetTargetProgram does not clear, stated on their own so the defect is not hidden inside a longer case
  note DEFECT, recorded not blessed. SetTargetProgram documents that changing the target discards everything read about the previous program, and it clears HasPAT, HasPMT, the PMT PID and every stream fact - but not pmtProgramNumber and not pmtVersion. So Facts reports programNumber=1 and pmtVersion=9 for a program that has been discarded, while HasPMT is false. Reset() clears both, so the two paths disagree. No current consumer reads either field without checking HasPMT first, which is why this is latent rather than live. It must be settled in a Go-reference PR before a Rust PSI parser is written against these lines, or the Rust core will be made to reproduce a stale value on purpose.
  init target=1
  chunk 
  facts through=376 hasPAT=1 hasPMT=1 pmtVersion=9 programNumber=1 pmtPID=256 videoPID=257 videoCodec=h264 audioPIDs=
  events identity identity
  psi pat=0 pmt=1
  target 2
  facts through=0 hasPAT=0 hasPMT=0 pmtVersion=9 programNumber=1 pmtPID=0 videoPID=0 videoCodec=unknown audioPIDs=
  events identity
  psi pat= pmt=
end

end
